agree.reason: The plain apology and the specific promises about weekly emails and weather credits answer exactly why this household left, but nothing makes up for the $540 year they lost, and there's no sign-up link to act on, so a resisting reader may still hold back.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief, and the email admits the nets' limited cover and the chance of crop loss, though "many of you said" glosses 29 of 41 respondents and "you won't pay for a half-empty box" leans a little past a credit rule that kicks in only above a one-third cut.

works_the_facts.reason: Nothing is worked out from the numbers: it doesn't give the weekly value of a share (about $24.50), what the six thin weeks cost a member (roughly $74), or the survey result as 29 of 41, so the reader never sees what the new credit is actually worth.

right_comparison.reason: Last year is described honestly as the thing being fixed, but the email never compares signing up with not signing up, and the 52 remaining shares are stated without any sense of how fast they're going.

qualification.reason: The more-than-a-third credit rule and the plain statement that loss can't be ruled out are concrete and something a member could check, though it doesn't say who decides a box was cut or how the credit is paid.

objections.reason: The two complaints, that the farm went quiet and paid nothing back, are each met with a specific promise, but the obvious follow-up about any credit for last year's thin boxes goes unanswered.

fit.reason: It's a short, clear email under 200 words, but it leaves out the website sign-up link and doesn't mention Thursday pickup.
